items.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: And it goes into all that with Charlie Parker and Bud Powell and all that stuff.

ctx.x: It’s unfortunate that jazz, especially in the 50s and somewhat in the 60s I guess, was associated with drug abuse and all that. And sometimes I tell people well look where people went to work. They went to work in a bar very often, and the surroundings.

Back then they didn’t know, like what they know now about excessive use of those drugs. Back then they didn’t really – it’s the same thing with smoking. Everybody smoked, right? Now like 60 or 70 years later, “Oh man it’s really bad. You shouldn’t smoke.” You know. But back then everybody was smoking. So, and I just finished reading the Miles Davis autobiography. And it goes into all that with Charlie Parker and Bud Powell and all that stuff. And, but what those guys were going through, it’s terrible. I mean it’d…
Did you resign from the trio?
